# judgekeeper

> Check your LLM-as-a-judge. See how often it agrees with human labels, in one command. An LLM-as-a-judge is an AI model that grades the answers of another AI model. judgekeeper is a free, open-source command-line tool that runs on your own computer.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.judgekeeper.com/): what judgekeeper is, how it works in three parts, the whole process in six steps, how to install it inside your project on Mac, Linux or Windows, and what you get
- [Guide](https://www.judgekeeper.com/start.html): check your judge step by step with `judgekeeper start`: install, connect your results, start, mark, your result, improve your judge; each step with what to type, what you will see, when you are done and what to do when it did not work; then the details: what it reads, what it never does, reviewing the disagreements, fixing your judge's rule (an AI assistant can do it and check the new rule with `--rule-file`), asking your judge again, trying your new judge, running it again, and results saved in your own format
- [Docs](https://www.judgekeeper.com/docs.html): every page in one list, grouped: start, your eval tool, your Python code, keys and security, the changelog and where to report a problem
- [Reference](https://www.judgekeeper.com/reference.html): every command, file format, option, exit code and config key
- [Setup and API keys](https://www.judgekeeper.com/setup.html): when a key is needed, and how to give one safely
- [How it works, in depth](https://www.judgekeeper.com/learn.html): why a judge needs checking, what the numbers mean, the tools it can read results from and a real result
